identity.title: Cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot enabling ultrasensitive one-pot detection of dual miRNAs in triple-negative breast cancer.

content.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are critical biomarkers for the early diagnosis of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but sensitive simultaneous detection of multiple miRNAs remains a clinical challenge. Herein, we report an innovative biosensing method based on a cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot for one-pot, rapid, and ultrasensitive dual miRNA detection. Target miRNAs trigger the cascade DNA walker, which integrates catalytic hairpin assembly and enzyme-mediated strand displacement, to generate abundant single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). These ssDNA then activate the photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot under light illumination, enabling amplified fluorescence signaling for dual-target quantification. The assay exhibits a linear range of 100 aM to 1 pM with a limit of detection of 48.7 aM. Serum recovery experiments and cell line tests confirm its reliability in complex matrices. Clinical validation using 30 plasma samples (15 TNBC patients, 15 healthy controls) demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve, AUC = 0.964). This method features simple operation and strong clinical translational potential, offering a reliable tool for the early diagnosis of TNBC.
